Theme

School & learning

spelling noun

also spell, spell a word, orthography, how do you spell it?

classical

Suet. Aug. 88.1
Quint. 1.4.17; 1.7.1
Traupman 31, 248
M-O s.v. spelling

orthographia, orthographiae f.

noun, first declension

spelling, orthography

The grammarians’ Greek word, ‘the rule and method of writing’ (Suet. Aug. 88.1), which Quintilian renders rēctē scrībendī scientia (1.7.1); Lewis & Short: post-Augustan. To spell is simply scrībere: rēctē scrībere, to spell correctly (Traupman 29, 248). Morgan–Owens: I’m terrible at spelling, orthographiam haudquāquam calleō.

Examples

  • Orthographiam, id est fōrmulam ratiōnemque scrībendī ā grammaticīs īnstitūtam, nōn adeō custōdiit

    He did not keep closely to spelling, that is, the rule and method of writing laid down by the grammariansSuet. Aug. 88.1

  • quod Graecī ὀρθογραφίαν vocant; hoc nōs rēctē scrībendī scientiam nōminēmus

    what the Greeks call orthography; let us call it the science of writing correctlyQuint. 1.7.1

  • Quōmodo scrībitur hoc verbum?

    How do you spell this word?composed

Other words

  • scrīptūra, scrīptūrae f. — the way a word is written, spelling

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 248; Caecin. ap. Cic. Fam. 6.7.1: mendum scrīptūrae, a slip in writing (Lewis & Short)

    Writing in general, and the written form of a word.

See also write, word, alphabet, capital letter, mistake, grammar.
